newsitem.title: UK: UK business confidence grows in Q2-survey.
newsitem.headline: UK business confidence grows in Q2-survey.

text.p: Business confidence among British managers rose in the second quarter with support for the new Labour government growing, a business survey said on Friday.

The Institute of Management's (IM) latest quarterly trends survey showed 64 percent of managers are optimistic about their companies' prospects, and almost four in 10 believe they will be better off financially in the year ahead.
The survey also found 70 percent feel secure in their job.
The honeymoon between business and the new Labour government continued in the second quarter with support among executives increasing to 30 percent from 20 percent at the time of the election in May.
The survey found part-time and full-time employment increased during the period, but noted inflationary pressures look set to increase.
Some 66 percent of firms said they were planning to hold prices steady with 28 percent planning price rises next quarter.
This compares with 20 percent of firms raising prices in the last quarter.
"This survey shows that the temperature of the economy continues to rise, as does anxiety about possible overheating," said Roger Young, IM director-general.
"Mangers are now in search of cooling waters to damp down the heat in the high street and take some steam out of the economy."
IM said 305 managers responded to this quarter's survey, conducted in the past week.
